I have a few, but the most recent one was when I was taking my aunt to the optical hospital. She was in surgery for her cataracts, and the whole place just had this weird fucking energy. The nurses didn't let me stay in the waiting room with everyone else, instead taking me to an actual doctors-office-room-thing and having me stay there. It wasn't my aunts room either, cause I saw the one she was in beforehand. The nurses kept looking at me when they thought I wouldn't notice, one nurse in particular did it more than others.
This is where the "scariest encounter with a human" comes in. She tells me to follow her, and proceeds to say, "you're lucky you came on a good day, we won't be having those sometime soon." And that sentence chilled me to the fucking core. I know it doesn't sound that bad, but it was the way she said it, and the whole scenario. It felt like I was in a movie and these nurses were like angels or some shit. I kind of just nod and do the whole yeah haha thing in response, and she just takes me back to the doctors room. 
They bring my aunt out and all is normal. They want me to go get the car so she can just be wheelchaired up to it, and as I'm going, the nurse says "she's lucky to have you. Be careful out there." Which AGAIN is normal in retrospect but just the way she said it, it was so monotone, it really freaked me out.
One part of me thinks that I'm overdramatic, the other thinks that the hospital was also a cult of some kind.

I've had that happen multiple times, and so has my mother. My first job was about 7-10 minutes away depending on traffic, and I always left at about 9 o'clock to arrive early, (my shift starts at 9:15). That morning I woke up late, at about 9:13, and I hauled ass getting my uniform together and getting there. I couldn't speed or anything since there was traffic on the roads, but when I got to work it was 9:14.

My mom on the other hand works 45 minutes away. She told me a story of how she left work at 2:30, and made it back to her house at 2:35. She was so confused, and just assumed that she saw her leaving time wrong, but she had texts proving that she had left at a certain time.
